title: Jude and the Confession
premise: True-crime podcaster Bram Pemberton is hired by a nervous woman named Jude to prove that her wealthy uncle Bram's namesake, Aldous Pemberton, will be murdered on his eightieth birthday — a crime that hasn't happened yet. Digging into the family's tangled trust, Bram discovers a forged confession buried in the estate archives that could rewrite who inherits everything, and realizes Jude herself may be both the predicted victim's heir and the killer's target. As the birthday approaches, Bram sets a trap using the confession as bait, forcing the killer — the family's trusted lawyer, who has been laundering the inheritance for decades — into a recorded confession of his own. The book ends with the murder prevented, the confession aired, and Bram realizing Jude hired him not to stop a crime but to make sure the truth had a witness.
about_author: Sable Okafor is a former estate paralegal who spent a decade watching families tear themselves apart over paper. They now write mysteries where the deadliest weapon is a signature.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Bram Pemberton's POV. A client named Jude retains Bram to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — her uncle Aldous, due to die on his eightieth birthday, three weeks away. Bram, broke and skeptical, takes the retainer. The emotional beat is wary curiosity curdling into unease when Jude pays far too much and knows too much about how Bram works.

chapters.title: The Paper Corpse
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, alternating with Jude's journal entries. Inside the Pemberton estate, Bram finds a sealed confession naming Aldous's first wife's death as murder — unsigned, undated, but legally devastating to the inheritance. Rising tension: someone ransacks Bram's studio the same night, taking everything except the confession copy. The beat is the thrill of the hunt shadowed by the sense of being hunted.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The birthday gala looms; Bram identifies the lawyer, Corwin Voss, as the only person with access to every version of the file — and the only beneficiary if the confession is destroyed. When Jude disappears, Bram realizes his client was bait all along, and the statute clock on the original crime expires at midnight of the birthday. The beat is desperation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Jude and the Confession
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax and resolution. At the gala, Bram springs the trap: the forged confession is read aloud as genuine, and Voss moves to destroy it — and its witness — on camera. Jude emerges alive, having engineered the whole scenario to force the truth into the open before the statute killed it forever. The beat is catharsis: justice delayed, but finally recorded.
